Estimate an Ising model

Source: R/build_aliases.R
build_ising.Rd

build_network(method = "ising"), or for short build_ising(), estimates an Ising model of binary variables. The edge between two variables is their interaction, fitted by L1-penalised logistic regression of each variable on the others, with the penalty chosen by EBIC, and the two estimates of each edge combined into one undirected weight (van Borkulo et al., 2014). It needs the glmnet package.

An edge is a conditional association between two variables given all the others; an absent edge means the penalty removed it.

Usage

build_ising(
  data,
  actor = NULL,
  ...,
  gamma = 0.25,
  nlambda = 100L,
  rule = c("AND", "OR"),
  metadata_cols = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  labels = NULL,
  params = list()
)

Arguments

data

The binary variables: a data frame with one row per observation and one column per variable, holding only 0 and 1. Non-numeric columns and a column named rid are set aside; columns with non-syntactic names, all-missing and constant columns, and rows with a missing value are dropped, each with a message; fewer than 2 variables or 3 complete rows, or any value other than 0 and 1, raise an error.

actor

An id column naming whose observation each row is; it is set aside, not modelled. Default NULL.

...

Further arguments for build_network(). method cannot be given (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

gamma

The EBIC hyperparameter. Default 0.25.

nlambda

The number of penalties tried. Default 100.

rule

"AND" (default) keeps an edge when both regressions select it, "OR" when either does.

metadata_cols

Columns to keep as the network's metadata (covariates), never read as variables. Default NULL.

group

A column to split the data by: one network per value, returned as a netobject_group. Default NULL.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" rescales the weights to run from 0 to 1, over every cell for the transition methods (tna's rule, so with no zero cell the smallest weight becomes 0) and over the non-zero weights, into (0, 1], for the other methods, "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1; an undirected network whose matrix it makes asymmetric becomes directed, so both of a pair's values are kept as edges. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none).

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names. Default NULL.

params

Settings for the estimator, as a named list. The network stores them, so the resampling verbs re-estimate with the same settings. Default list().

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group), as build_network() returns it.

References

van Borkulo, C. D., Borsboom, D., Epskamp, S., Blanken, T. F., Boschloo, L., Schoevers, R. A., & Waldorp, L. J. (2014). A new method for constructing networks from binary data. Scientific Reports, 4, 5918. doi:10.1038/srep05918

See also

build_network() for every method; build_mgm() for mixed continuous and categorical variables.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  binary <- data.frame(matrix(rbinom(200, 1, 0.5), ncol = 5))
  build_network(binary, method = "ising")
  build_ising(binary, rule = "OR")
}
#> Ising Model Network [undirected]
#>   Sample size: 40
#> 
#>   No edges: every weight is zero.
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix.
#> 
#>   Gamma: 0.25  |  Rule: OR
#>   Thresholds: [-0.201, 0.405]
